cards.name_on_card: I am the poet and traveller of 1883
cards.summary: Lined notebook paper containing handwritten text written in pencil and ink.
cards.typed_words:
[Leftmost page]
June 2, 1873
I am the poet and traveller of 1883
Leaving my homeland across the Deep
waters of the great Pacific Sea
All the way from Peking
Towards the mountains filled with gold
It's all there for the taking
Say Tello the tales that I've been told
The sea has calmed enough to sail
Captain find us San Francisco
Towards the mountains filled with gold.

June 2, 1877
The pig has been sold as my hands bleed
The wind now blows cold in my disbelief
Seeking success yet still waiting to succeed
Dreams unfufilled and America the thief
Set foot upon the shore,
Knowing not what was instore
Sadness, Discrimination
Found in my new Nation
Feeling so alone and still I am poor
Still paying my way
But I might regret it some day

[Top middle page]
June 2 1882

[Bottom middle page]
June 2, 1878
The tracks are being laid
And I'm barely getting paid
Outcasted and shunned by my countrymen
Attempt to cut my hair, barely one a gentlemen
So much steal has been made
That something has been stolen
The sinking sunset over the Pacific fades
The summer sun shines so golden
The only gold I see

June 2, 1879
My people and I continue to pursue the
American Dream
So far unseen yet we wait in hope
To make wise our voyage by boat
In seeking escape from a crumbling ruin
As the Chinese Empire the shadows doom
We stay to ourselves silent to the whiteman's sound
Living in safety in our China towns
Keep alive the memories of our kin
Waiting for gold while being served Tin
Shackled to a railroad hammering the ground
Working in sadness, cold irons bound
Living in exile in our chinaman towns

[Rightmost page]
June 2, 1880
What have I to live for with no family of my own
Except for desolation, silently sad and alone
Dreaming of my ancestors happy to stay home
The life of a chinese
a life of unease [...cut for the check]
